dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Patriots Turn to Tommy DeVito Following Drake Maye Fibula Fracture
dailyTopNewsBrief.summary: New England (5-5) enters Week 12 facing a significant roster shift after rookie quarterback Drake Maye suffered a season-threatening leg injury. Currently holding the AFC's #8 seed, the team must stabilize an offense averaging 2.0 giveaways per game to maintain their 38.3% playoff probability.
bullets: Quarterback Drake Maye is confirmed out with a fractured right fibula, while wideout A.J. Brown is doubtful for the upcoming slate due to a hamstring injury [S10](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50542578/patriots-qb-drake-maye-fractured-fibula-sources-say)

With Maye sidelined, the Patriots will transition to Tommy DeVito at quarterback to navigate a remaining schedule that features several top-tier NFL opponents [S8](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50503981/drake-maye-ankle-injury-patriots-tommy-devito-stats)

Financial analysis indicates the team's 5-5 record stems from underperformance among top earners, though the unit maintains a #8 ranked defensive sack rate of 7.8% [S4](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50544188/new-england-patriots-highest-paid-players-2026)

Tight end Hunter Henry remains focused on the team's mindset heading into the final seven games, as New England looks to improve a #31 ranked -10 turnover differential [S13](https://www.patriots.com/video/one-on-one-with-hunter-henry-patriots-all-access)
